synopsis: VVM, the follow-on to PEGASUS, ran from July 2019 to June 2023 with a reported EUR 47 million project volume, representing a second four-year capability-building cycle in that programme family [f1205, f1292, f1549]. The booklet uses VVM and related programmes as a reference class for schedule forecasting and concludes that validation capability took years to build in every documented case; these are on-road precedents, not direct off-road evidence [f15717, f15713, f9614]. VVM developed verification and validation methods for urban Level 4 and 5 automation and sought a significant shift from real tests to simulation, but retained proving-ground and field testing [f1548, f1777]. Another account groups PEGASUS and VVM as validating methods rather than products for Level 3 and 4 cars, creating a scope tension; consortium acceptance was reported, but no approval or post-capability validation duration was reported [f1772, f1778, f1776]. Confidence is limited by consortium self-reporting despite “Independent” labels, and later chapters explicitly treat VVM as unverified and recommend checking it before reliance or review [f1294, f4336, f7701, f11276].
